about.title: Willows Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Willows is a small community, but its roads carry a steady stream of local and through traffic, especially along Interstate 5 Northbound, W Wood Street, Sycamore Street, and Route 162. Public records show crashes here tend to cluster on Wednesdays around the late-morning to early-afternoon hours, often tied to commuting and errand traffic near town. Even a single injury collision can upend daily life in a town this size, from missed work at a local business to mounting medical bills at the nearest clinic or hospital. LawProactive helps Glenn County residents find an independent personal injury attorney who understands rural highway crashes and the challenges of dealing with insurers after a wreck. There's no charge to connect, and the attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning you owe nothing unless your case results in a recovery. We're not a law firm, and we don't decide your case, but we can help you find someone who will listen and explain your options.

items.title: Time Limits Matter
items.desc: California generally allows two years from the crash date to file a claim, but that window can shrink to as little as six months if a government entity, such as Glenn County or Caltrans, may be responsible for road conditions on I-5 or Route 162. Acting early helps preserve your options.

items.title: Comparative Fault Still Pays
items.desc: California follows a pure comparative fault rule, meaning you can still recover damages even if you were partly at fault for the collision. An attorney can help make sure your share of blame is fairly assessed, not overstated by an insurer.

items.title: No Cap on What You've Lost
items.desc: California places no cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering in most car accident cases. An independent attorney can help document how the crash has affected your daily life, not just your medical bills.

items.question: Should I give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurance company?
items.answer: It's generally wise to avoid giving a recorded statement before speaking with an attorney. Insurers often use these statements to look for ways to reduce or deny a claim. An independent attorney can help you understand what, if anything, you need to say.

items.question: What if my crash happened on Interstate 5 near Willows and involved a state or county vehicle?
items.answer: Claims against a government entity, like Caltrans or Glenn County, follow much shorter deadlines than typical personal injury cases, sometimes as little as six months. It's important to get legal guidance quickly if a government vehicle or road defect was involved. Waiting too long can forfeit your right to file at all.

items.question: How much does it cost to use LawProactive?
items.answer: Connecting with an attorney through LawProactive is completely free. Attorneys in our network work on contingency, so there's no upfront cost, and you only pay if your case results in a recovery. LawProactive itself is not a law firm and does not charge any fees.
